facts.f: Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level.
facts.e: In 2020, Nepal and China announced its height as 8,848.86 metres.

facts.f: The Nile is usually listed as the longest river, at about 6,650 km.
facts.e: Some scientists argue that the Amazon is a little longer, depending on where you measure from.

facts.f: The Amazon carries more water than any other river.
facts.e: It pours more water into the sea than the next several biggest rivers put together.

facts.f: The Amazon rainforest is the largest tropical rainforest in the world.
facts.e: It is home to an enormous number of plant and animal species.

facts.f: The Caspian Sea is the largest lake in the world by area.
facts.e: Even though it is called a sea, it is a lake because it is surrounded by land. Its water is salty.

facts.f: Lake Superior in North America is the largest freshwater lake by area.
facts.e: It is one of the five Great Lakes.

facts.f: Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest and oldest lake in the world.
facts.e: It holds about a fifth of all the unfrozen fresh water on Earth's surface.

facts.f: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the world's highest waterfall.
facts.e: Its total drop is 979 metres, including one unbroken plunge of about 807 metres.

facts.f: Greenland is the largest island in the world.
facts.e: Australia is bigger, but it is counted as a continent.

facts.f: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest place on dry land.
facts.e: It lies more than 400 metres below sea level.

facts.f: The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth.
facts.e: Some weather stations there have recorded almost no rain for many years.

facts.f: The coldest air temperature ever measured by a weather station was −89.2 °C.
facts.e: It was recorded at Vostok Station in Antarctica in 1983.

facts.f: The Andes in South America is the longest mountain range on land.
facts.e: It runs for about 7,000 km along the western side of the continent.

facts.f: The Himalayas have the world's highest peaks.
facts.e: All of the world's mountains over 8,000 metres are in the Himalaya and Karakoram ranges.

facts.f: Majuli, in the Brahmaputra River in Assam, is one of the largest river islands in the world.
facts.e: It is a centre of Assamese culture and its monasteries, called satras.

facts.f: Chilika Lake in Odisha is India's largest coastal lagoon.
facts.e: In winter, it hosts huge flocks of migratory birds.

facts.f: Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia.
facts.e: The Jhelum River flows into and out of it.

facts.f: The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta is the largest river delta in the world.
facts.e: It covers much of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

facts.f: The Brahmaputra is called the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet.
facts.e: It enters India in Arunachal Pradesh, where it is called the Siang.

facts.f: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the highest mountain in Africa.
facts.e: It is a dormant volcano, about 5,895 metres high.

facts.f: Measured from its base on the sea floor, Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller than Everest.
facts.e: Most of it is underwater. From base to top it is over 10,000 metres.

facts.f: The summit of Mount Chimborazo in Ecuador is the point on Earth farthest from Earth's centre.
facts.e: Earth bulges at the Equator, and Chimborazo sits near the Equator.

facts.f: Russia and China each share land borders with 14 countries.
facts.e: That is more than any other country.

facts.f: Lake Titicaca, between Peru and Bolivia, is often called the highest navigable lake.
facts.e: It lies about 3,800 metres above sea level, and large boats sail on it.

facts.f: In Nepal, Mount Everest is called Sagarmatha. In Tibet, it is called Chomolungma.
facts.e: It was named Everest by the British after George Everest, a surveyor.

facts.f: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary were the first to reach the top of Mount Everest, on 29 May 1953.
facts.e: Tenzing was a Sherpa mountaineer and Hillary was a beekeeper and climber from New Zealand.

facts.f: Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest, in 1984.
facts.e: She reached the summit on 23 May 1984.

facts.f: Junko Tabei of Japan was the first woman to climb Mount Everest, in 1975.
facts.e: She later climbed the highest peak on every continent.

facts.f: Dong, in Arunachal Pradesh, is where the Sun rises first in India.
facts.e: Arunachal Pradesh is often called the 'Land of the Dawn-lit Mountains'.

facts.f: Indira Point in the Nicobar Islands is the southernmost point of India.
facts.e: Kanyakumari is the southern tip of mainland India.

facts.f: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa.
facts.e: It is one of the sources of the River Nile.

facts.f: Australia is both a country and a continent.
facts.e: It is the only country that covers a whole continent.

facts.f: Kangchenjunga, on the India–Nepal border, is the third-highest mountain in the world.
facts.e: It is about 8,586 metres high.

facts.f: K2 is the second-highest mountain in the world.
facts.e: It is in the Karakoram range and is known as one of the hardest mountains to climb.

facts.f: The Sahara was once green.
facts.e: Between about 11,000 and 5,000 years ago, it had lakes, grasslands and animals like hippos.

facts.f: Antarctica holds about 70% of the world's fresh water, frozen as ice.
facts.e: If all its ice melted, sea levels would rise by many metres.

facts.f: Canada has the longest coastline of any country.
facts.e: It has many islands in the Arctic, which add a lot of coastline.

facts.f: Africa lies in all four hemispheres: northern, southern, eastern and western.
facts.e: Both the Equator and the Prime Meridian cross Africa.

facts.f: Istanbul is a city on two continents.
facts.e: The Bosporus strait divides it into a European part and an Asian part.

facts.f: The main stretch of the Amazon River has no bridges across it.
facts.e: It flows mostly through thick rainforest with few roads, and its banks change often.

facts.f: The Atlantic Ocean gets a few centimetres wider every year.
facts.e: The plates on either side of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge are slowly moving apart.

facts.f: Jog Falls in Karnataka is one of India's highest plunge waterfalls.
facts.e: The Sharavathi River drops about 253 metres there.

quiz.q: Which is the highest mountain above sea level?
quiz.x: Everest is 8,848.86 metres high.

quiz.q: Which is the largest island in the world?
quiz.x: Greenland is the largest island. Australia is bigger, but it is counted as a continent.

quiz.q: Which is the highest waterfall that falls without a break?
quiz.x: Angel Falls in Venezuela has an unbroken plunge of about 807 metres.

quiz.q: Which is the largest tropical rainforest?
quiz.x: The Amazon rainforest is in South America.

quiz.q: Which river carries the most water?
quiz.x: The Nile is usually called the longest, but the Amazon carries the most water.

quiz.q: Which is the largest lake in the world by area?
quiz.x: The Caspian Sea is a salty lake surrounded by land.

quiz.q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
quiz.x: Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest and oldest lake.

quiz.q: Which is the longest mountain range on land?
quiz.x: The Andes run about 7,000 km along South America.

quiz.q: Who first reached the top of Mount Everest in 1953?
quiz.x: They reached the summit on 29 May 1953.

quiz.q: Who was the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest?
quiz.x: Bachendri Pal reached the top on 23 May 1984.

quiz.q: What is Mount Everest called in Nepal?
quiz.x: Chomolungma is its Tibetan name.

quiz.q: Which is the highest mountain in Africa?
quiz.x: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is about 5,895 metres high.

quiz.q: Which is the largest river delta in the world?
quiz.x: It covers much of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

quiz.q: Where is the lowest place on dry land?
o: The shore of the Dead Sea
quiz.x: The Dead Sea shore is more than 400 metres below sea level.

quiz.q: Where was the coldest temperature on Earth's surface recorded?
quiz.x: −89.2 °C was recorded at Vostok Station in Antarctica in 1983.

quiz.q: In which Indian state does the Sun rise first?
quiz.x: Dong village in Arunachal Pradesh sees India's first sunrise.

quiz.q: What is the southernmost point of India?
quiz.x: Indira Point is in the Nicobar Islands. Kanyakumari is the tip of the mainland.

quiz.q: Which is India's largest coastal lagoon?
quiz.x: Chilika Lake is in Odisha.

quiz.q: What is the Brahmaputra called in Tibet?
quiz.x: It becomes the Siang in Arunachal Pradesh and the Brahmaputra in Assam.

quiz.q: What is Majuli?
o: A large river island in Assam
quiz.x: Majuli lies in the Brahmaputra River.

quiz.q: Which mountain is taller than Everest if measured from its base on the sea floor?
quiz.x: Mauna Kea in Hawaii is over 10,000 metres from base to top.

quiz.q: Which is the second-highest mountain in the world?
quiz.x: K2 is in the Karakoram range. Kangchenjunga is third.
